title: Bursa
description: A named synovial bursa (or a small number of anatomically well-established, unnamed-but-constant bursae described in the surgical literature) -- a fluid-filled sac reducing friction between a tendon/muscle and adjacent bone or another tendon. Distinct from schema/fascia.schema.json's retinacula/fibrous tunnels: a bursa is a synovial-lined potential space, not a fibrous sheet, and 'bursitis' plus real ultrasound/fluoroscopy-guided bursal aspiration and corticosteroid/PRP injection are common, distinct clinical procedures from either a muscle motor-point injection or a tendon-substance injection.

adjacent_structures.description: ids or plain-text names of the tendon(s)/muscle(s)/bone(s) this bursa lies between or deep to -- an id where this atlas already models the structure, plain text otherwise.

communicates_with_joint.description: whether this bursa's cavity is documented to communicate with an adjacent synovial joint in a meaningful proportion of individuals (e.g. the subacromial-subdeltoid bursa does not communicate with the glenohumeral joint in a healthy shoulder, but the pisotriquetral joint often communicates with the radiocarpal joint) -- clinically relevant because a communicating bursa can spread an infection or an injectate into the joint.

clinical_significance.description: the named clinical entity this bursa is most associated with (e.g. 'subacromial bursitis / rotator cuff impingement', 'prepatellar bursitis (housemaid's knee)').

injection_approach.description: How this bursa is found and safely aspirated/injected under ultrasound -- the bursal counterpart of a muscle's ultrasound_injection_approach or a tendon's prp_injection_approach. Populated only where real, citable clinical literature exists.
